items.title: Postal trade unions and employers call for strong minimum standards in EU Delivery Act
items.summary: As the European Commission drafts its EU Delivery Act, a reform that will determine the future of post and the jobs of 1.8 million postal workers, postal companies and union have agreed on the pillars of a future-proof framework: a functioning universal service, sustainable networks in the e-commerce era and quality jobs for all workers The post Postal trade unions and employers call for strong minimum standards in EU Delivery Act appeared first on UNI Global Union .

items.title: Make Amazon Pay Day 2026: Amazon workers and supporters to strike and protest in over 20 countries as union wins first North American collective agreement
items.summary: Amazon workers and their allies will strike and protest in over 20 countries from Black Friday, 27 November, to Cyber Monday, 30 November 2026, two weeks after warehouse workers in British Columbia secured the first binding union contract for Amazon workers anywhere in North America. items.title: “They don’t realise how strong we are together”: Barnsley nursery workers strike to protect children and pensions
items.summary: Thirty care workers, all of them women organised in the GMB union, are taking action against Barnsley Council’s plan to hand its council-run nurseries to a private provider in January 2027. They are among the lowest-paid workers in Britain. Many work part-time or term time only. items.title: Organizing wins Hungary’s social care workers a pay rise, SZÁD says they will keep fighting for more
items.summary: Social care workers in Hungary will receive a 15 per cent gross pay increase from January 2027, after years of organizing and mobilizing by their union, SZÁD. Workers fought for this gain. items.title: AI, Automation, and Fiscal Pressure
items.summary: We study how automation affects public finances in countries that (i) tax labor at a higher rate than capital and (ii) fund services such as health care and education from tax revenues rather than user fees. We embed task-level automation within a two-sector general equilibrium model, which we calibrate to match data from EU countries. Automation shifts income toward more lightly taxed capital. If public services follow consumer demand, the budget deficit worsens at unchanged tax rates, even if automation is as fast in the public-service sector as in the private sector. In our EU-27 benchmark scenario, where automation proceeds faster in the market sector, the deficit rises by nearly one percentage point of value added as the economy grows by twelve percent due to automation.
